title: Geometric irreducibility detected by the generic residue field
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $X$ an irreducible $k$-scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-irreducible-components]. Let $\xi$ be its generic point, meaning $\overline{\{\xi\}}=|X|$ [def-sc-generic-point], and give its residue field $\kappa(\xi)$ [def-weil-residue-field] the induced $k$-algebra structure. Then $X$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$ if and only if $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\xi)$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. No reducedness or finite-type hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Put $Y=X_{\mathrm{red}}$ and let $i:Y\to X$ be its reduction map. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism], $Y$ is reduced and $i$ is a surjective closed immersion inducing a homeomorphism after every base change. Its homeomorphism identifies the unique point $\eta$ above $\xi$ as a generic point and makes $Y$ irreducible. For every field extension $L/k$ it identifies $|Y_L|$ with $|X_L|$, so $Y$ is geometrically irreducible if and only if $X$ is. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-residue-field-iso], $i$ induces an isomorphism $\kappa(\xi)\to\kappa(\eta)$; this is a $k$-algebra isomorphism because the structure map of $Y$ is the composite through $X$. Thus it suffices to prove the equivalence for $Y$.

source.place: Tag 054Q, proof of (2) implies (1), reduction to the reduced scheme; the same reduction may be made before both implications

proof.text: The reduced irreducible scheme $Y$ is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Write $K=\mathcal O_{Y,\eta}$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], $K$ is a field and every nonempty affine open $U\subseteq Y$ contains $\eta$, with $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_Y)$ a domain embedded in $K$ by the germ map. Since the maximal ideal of a field is zero, the residue-field definition identifies $K=\kappa(\eta)$, compatibly with $k$. The nonempty affine opens, ordered by reverse inclusion, form a nonempty directed poset: for two such opens their intersection contains $\eta$ and has an affine neighbourhood of $\eta$. They are cofinal among all open neighbourhoods of $\eta$, since affine opens form a basis of a scheme. The stalk description [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] therefore gives $K=\varinjlim_{U}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_Y)$ as $k$-algebras: every germ has an affine representative, and equality of two germs holds on a neighbourhood which can again be shrunk to an affine neighbourhood of $\eta$.

proof.text: Assume $Y$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$. By [lem-zl-geometric-irreducibility-affine-local], every nonempty affine open $U$ has geometrically irreducible coordinate $k$-algebra $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_Y)$. Apply clause (2) of [lem-zl-geometric-irreducibility-subalgebra-colimit] to the directed diagram in step 2. Its colimit $K$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$. Since $K=\kappa(\eta)$, this proves the forward implication for $Y$.

source.place: Tag 054Q, proof of (1) implies (2), application of Tags 038G and 037N to the affine-neighbourhood colimit

proof.text: Conversely, assume $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$. Identify this residue field with $K$ as in step 2. For every nonempty affine open $U\subseteq Y$, [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] supplies the injective $k$-algebra germ map $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_Y)\to K$. Clause (1) of [lem-zl-geometric-irreducibility-subalgebra-colimit] implies that its source is geometrically irreducible over $k$. Applying the converse direction of [lem-zl-geometric-irreducibility-affine-local] to the irreducible scheme $Y$ shows that $Y$ is geometrically irreducible.

proof.text: Steps 3 and 4 give $Y$ geometrically irreducible over $k$ if and only if $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)$ is geometrically irreducible over $k$. The equivalence and the $k$-algebra residue-field isomorphism in step 1 transfer the two sides to $X$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\xi)$ respectively, proving the assertion for the original, possibly nonreduced scheme.
